# Culturix video generation — architecture, operations, and hard-won gotchas

**Status: current as of 2026-09-02.** Unlike `CLAUDE.md` (regenerated by a
scheduled scan, so manual edits there get overwritten), this file is
hand-maintained and safe to add to. Update it when the video path changes.

This document exists because the video pipeline has repeatedly broken in
ways that were **invisible until an expensive generation failed** — and
several of those failures recurred because the reason was never written
down. If you read one section, read [Recurring failure patterns](#recurring-failure-patterns).

---

## 1. Three video paths, and which one runs

| Path | Model | Entry point | When it runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kling Omni** | Kling (hosted API) | `app/services/culturetoon_video.py` | provider `kling_omni` |
| **Self-hosted LTX-2.3** | `ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors` | `culturetoon_selfhosted_video.generate_toon_video_selfhosted` | provider `self_hosted`, `LTX_MODEL_VERSION` ≠ `2.5` |
| **Self-hosted LTX-2.5** | `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-*` | `culturetoon_selfhosted_video.generate_toon_video_ltx25` | provider `self_hosted`, **`LTX_MODEL_VERSION=2.5`** |

Both self-hosted paths run on the same RunPod Serverless endpoint. The
switch is `use_ltx25()` and is read in **two** places — the interactive
button (`app/routers/culturetoons.py::generate_toon_video`) and the
scheduled batch (`culturetoon_selfhosted_batch.py`). Changing one without
the other means manual and scheduled videos silently render on different
models.

### Why 2.5 replaced 2.3

2.3 output was rejected as unusable: no lip-sync, near-static motion,
visible artifacts. Two of those were **architectural**, not tuning:

- **Audio could never sync on 2.3.** Narration was synthesized separately
  (Chatterbox TTS) and muxed on with ffmpeg afterwards, so video and audio
  never informed each other. 2.5 denoises audio and video **jointly** in
  one pass (`LTXVEmptyLatentAudio` → `LTXVConcatAVLatent` → sampled
  together → `LTXVSeparateAVLatent` → `LTXVAudioVAEDecode`).
- **Continuity was faked on 2.3** by chaining each shot off the previous
  shot's last frame. 2.5 does multishot natively in one generation.

Measured, same script: **2.3 ≈ 1606s and ~$2.00, no audio. 2.5 ≈ 226s and
~$0.20–0.35, with native 48kHz stereo.** Roughly 7× faster and 6–10×
cheaper, for output the product owner rated "really good".

---

## 2. LTX-2.5: no LoRAs

**Character identity comes from image conditioning, not a trained LoRA.**
LTX-2.5 begins generation from a supplied first frame and propagates what
is in it. For several characters, `ltx25_workflow.build_composite_anchor()`
pastes each cast member's real portrait side by side into one
1280×704 frame, ordered left→right to match the blocking named in the prompt.

Consequences:

- No per-character training (~90 min GPU each).
- **Nothing to redo on a model upgrade.** LoRAs are version-locked —
  Lightricks: *"a LoRA only works with the model it was trained on"* — so a
  LoRA cast would need full retraining on every future LTX release.
- The real precondition is a **portrait per character** (`CharacterVariant.image_url`),
  which the router now enforces instead of `lora_status == "ready"`.

The 2.3 LoRA machinery (`culturetoon_lora.py`, training pods, the
inference-volume sync) is **left intact and unused** under 2.5. It still
works if `LTX_MODEL_VERSION` is unset.

Open question: identity drift over longer durations, since the anchor is
only the *first* frame. Verified good at 12s / 4 shots; untested beyond.

## 3. Environment variables

### Required for LTX-2.5 rendering
| Variable | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `LTX_MODEL_VERSION` | `2.5` | Absent/other ⇒ the 2.3 path |
| `RUNPOD_API_KEY` | — | |
| `RUNPOD_SERVERLESS_ENDPOINT_ID` | `wq8vb0ozn2gon7` | endpoint `culturix-eu-nl-1` |
| `RUNPOD_INFERENCE_NETWORK_VOLUME_ID` | `d65lm04dqr` | EU-NL-1, the volume the endpoint mounts |

### Only used by 2.3 LoRA training
`RUNPOD_NETWORK_VOLUME_ID` (`1zm4s72ecv`, EU-RO-1 — the **training/cache**
volume, a different volume), `RUNPOD_S3_*`, `HF_TOKEN`,
`LTX_TRAINING_CHECKPOINT_REPO/FILE`, `LTX_TRAINING_TEXT_ENCODER_REPO`,
`LTX_TRAINING_VIDEO_VAE_FILE`, `LTX_TRAINING_AUDIO_VAE_FILE`.

> **`RUNPOD_NETWORK_VOLUME_ID` and `RUNPOD_INFERENCE_NETWORK_VOLUME_ID` are
> two different volumes in two different datacenters.** Conflating them cost
> three days: every trained LoRA landed on EU-RO-1 while inference read from
> EU-NL-1, `lora_status` said `ready`, and nothing errored.

### Optional
`LTX25_WORKFLOW_PATH`, `LTX_WORKFLOW_PATH`, `RUNPOD_ALLOCATION_MAX_RETRIES`,
`RUNPOD_ALLOCATION_BACKOFF_SECONDS`.

## 4. Models on the volume (EU-NL-1 `d65lm04dqr`, ~38GB)

| File | Folder | Loader |
|---|---|---|
| `ltx-2.5-22b-distilled-transformer-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors` | `models/diffusion_models/` | `UNETLoader` |
| `gemma4-12b-with-proj-ltx-2.5-comfy-int8-convrot.safetensors` | `models/text_encoders/` | `CLIPLoader` |
| `ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors` | `models/vae/` | `VAELoader` |
| `ltx-2.5-audio-vae-bf16.safetensors` | `models/vae/` | `VAELoader` |
| `ltx-2.5-latent-spatial-upscaler-x2-bf16-1.0.safetensors` | `models/latent_upscale_models/` | `LatentUpscaleModelLoader` |

Re-download with `scripts/download_ltx25_to_volume.sh` **from a pod with the
volume mounted** — never via a laptop round-trip (that made each LoRA file
take ~30 min during the volume migration; pod-side the 21GB transformer
landed in ~2 min).

The optional prompt-enhancer CLIP (`gemma4_e2b_it_int8_convrot.safetensors`)
is **deliberately not downloaded**. `ltx25_workflow` points every
`CLIPLoader` at the main encoder and disables enhancement, because ComfyUI
validates every node feeding an output and rejects an unknown filename even
on an unused node.

## 5. The workflow graph

`app/media/workflows/ltx25_official/` holds the **unmodified** official
Comfy-Org templates. `app/media/workflows/ltx25_image_to_video.api.json` is
the API-format conversion actually used at runtime.

**Never hand-simplify these.** The LTX-2.3 workflow was hand-built down from
~44 nodes to ~10, which silently dropped `LTXVConditioning` — the node that
supplies frame-rate conditioning. Without it LTX gets no timing signal and
produces "a collection of images" rather than animation. That went
undiagnosed for weeks.

### Regenerating the API-format graph
```bash
python scripts/convert_comfy_workflow.py \
  --input app/media/workflows/ltx25_official/video_ltx2_5_i2v.json \
  --output app/media/workflows/ltx25_image_to_video.api.json \
  --object-info object_info.json
```
`object_info.json` comes from a live ComfyUI that has the LTX-2.5 nodes.
The serverless image has **no SSH**, so fetch it through the endpoint:
```json
{"input": {"debug_object_info": true, "classes": ["UNETLoader", "..."]}}
```

### Two required runtime deviations
Both established empirically; both live in `ltx25_workflow.build_workflow`:

1. **`ResizeImageMaskNode` is removed** and its consumers rewired. Its
   `resize_type` is a `COMFY_DYNAMICCOMBO_V3`; a
   `{"value": ..., "longer_size": ...}` dict passes ComfyUI's *validator*
   but execution then fails with `execute() missing 1 required positional
   argument: 'resize_type'`. Safe because the anchor is pre-sized to
   1280×704 — nothing in the sampling path changes.
2. **`SaveVideo.format`/`codec` are set explicitly.** The converter's schema
   walk doesn't surface them, and execution otherwise reaches the very last
   node and dies.

## 6. Recurring failure patterns

These recurred. Check them first.

### 6.1 Generated-but-never-read fields
The single most common bug in this codebase. A field is produced and then
silently dropped by the consumer:
- `shot.expression` — generated for weeks, never read by the prompt builder.
- `ToonBackground.country` / `.visual_style` — real columns, never read.
- `chatterbox_error` / `narration_mux_error` — the handler reported them;
  the client discarded them, so silent videos had no visible cause.

**Rule: ship the producer and consumer in the same commit, with a test for
both.** `lighting`/`blocking` were added this way.

### 6.2 Prompts inventing data that exists in the DB
- Locations had the script's **joke premise** as `name` and a run-on list of
  **character actions** as `description`, because `_script_scene_description`
  falls back to concatenating shot `action` lines. Fixed by
  `culturetoon_script.derive_scene_setting()`.
- A hand-written prompt described **Wen as a woman**; `characters.description`
  says *"A Chinese man"*. **Under 2.5 this also produces the wrong VOICE**,
  since audio is generated jointly. On 2.3 it couldn't, because narration
  used a separately chosen TTS voice.

`characters.description` is the usable field — `character_variants.description`
is empty and `culture_tag` is NULL for every character checked.

### 6.3 Verifying the wrong thing
- `verify_exists()` checked the **same volume it had just written to**, so it
  could never detect a wrong-volume upload.
- File **size** matching was treated as proof of integrity; a wrong-sized
  Aisha LoRA and a byte-identical-but-corrupt Kumar file both slipped through.
  **Use hashes, and validate a `.safetensors` by actually loading it.**

### 6.4 A running worker does not pull a rebuilt image
After any image rebuild, drain to zero (`workersMax=0`, wait for 0 workers)
then scale back up. A retry fix once appeared not to work purely because the
old image was still running.

### 6.5 409 Conflict right after an endpoint config change
RunPod rejects submissions for a while after a `workersMin/Max` PATCH. It's a
settling window, not a failure — retry with backoff.

### 6.6 Capacity, and the speed/availability trade
`throttled` workers mean RunPod has no capacity for the endpoint's GPU pool
in its region. Widening the pool helps availability but can cost speed —
A6000/L40 are markedly slower than H100. Current pool: H100 ×3, A100 ×2,
RTX PRO 6000 ×3, **L40S** (≈H100 for diffusion at ~5× lower cost).
The endpoint is pinned to EU-NL-1 because that is where the volume lives.

### 6.7 Docker base bumps and torch's local version
`5.10.0-base` ships `torch==2.11.0+cu128`. `pip freeze` captures the `+cu128`
local version, which **PyPI does not have** — the restore step must use
PyTorch's own CUDA index. **Never strip the suffix**: PyPI's plain torch is
the **CPU** build, and installing it over CUDA torch is what caused
`undefined symbol: ncclCommResume` to crash-loop every worker.

---

## 7. Operations

```bash
# Health / capacity
curl -s "https://api.runpod.ai/v2/$EP/health" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"

# Scale down (stop all spend)
curl -s -X PATCH "https://rest.runpod.io/v1/endpoints/$EP" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"workersMin":0,"workersMax":0}'

# Balance / burn rate
curl -s "https://api.runpod.io/graphql?api_key=$KEY" \
  -d '{"query":"query { myself { clientBalance currentSpendPerHr } }"}' \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

# Clear a stuck queue
curl -s -X POST "https://api.runpod.ai/v2/$EP/purge-queue" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

Resting cost is ~$0.039/hr baseline. `workersStandby` is **not settable via
the REST API** — console only.

Always terminate rented pods in a `finally`, but **never terminate on a
monitoring/printing error**: a `UnicodeEncodeError` in a progress print once
killed a running 40GB download because cleanup sat in `finally`.

---

## 8. Debugging a failed generation, in order

1. **`Toon.generation_error`** in the DB — usually the specific cause.
2. **RunPod endpoint logs** (console → Logs). The API exposes no worker
   stdout; ComfyUI's real error only appears here.
3. **ComfyUI validation errors are precise** — they name the node, the input
   and the received value. Read them literally.
4. **GitHub Actions build logs need repo admin.** A non-admin token gets 403,
   so ask the repo owner rather than guessing at build failures.

---

## 9. Known gaps

- **The full path through the website has not been exercised on 2.5.** All
  validation so far was direct API calls.
- **Identity drift beyond ~12s / 4 shots is untested.**
- **Aisha's LoRA is corrupt at source** (three fresh S3 downloads all failed
  `safe_open`). Moot while on 2.5; needs retraining if 2.3 is ever revived.
- **Background images** were generated from the old malformed Location
  descriptions. Only the text fields were regenerated. Matters for Kling,
  which uses `image_url` as a real `refer_image`; the self-hosted path never
  reads it.
- **Chatterbox mux and last-frame chaining are dead code under 2.5**, kept
  because the live 2.3 path still uses them.
- **`HF_TOKEN` was exposed in a pod's process list** during a download —
  worth rotating.
- **No QA pass on the self-hosted path** (the Kling path has one).

### Frontend still assumes the pre-2.5 world
The character setup UI has not caught up, and currently instructs users to
do unnecessary work:

| Location | Problem under 2.5 |
|---|---|
| `CharacterVariantManager.tsx` "Kling character registration" | Copy says *"Required before generating any video"* — **false** under 2.5, where identity comes from the portrait anchor. Only true for the Kling Omni path. |
| Same panel's voice dropdown ("Auto (Kling picks a voice)" / ElevenLabs) | Under 2.5 the voice is produced by joint audio generation and is driven by `characters.description`, not by this control. |
| `CharacterVariantManager.tsx` LoRA training card | LoRAs are not used under 2.5 at all. |
| `GettingStartedChecklist.tsx` | Marks a setup step done only when `element_status === "ready"`, so it pushes users toward Kling registration they don't need. |

What a character actually needs under 2.5 is **a portrait**
(`CharacterVariant.image_url`) — which is what the API now enforces.

**Resolved 2026-09-02.** `GET /api/culturetoons/config` reports the active
renderer and what it requires; `ToonManager`, `CharacterVariantManager` and
`GettingStartedChecklist` all read it. Under 2.5 the Generate button gates on
a portrait, Step 2 shows an explicit ready/not-ready card, and the Kling +
Expressions + LoRA controls are collapsed behind an "Advanced" disclosure
(kept, because they remain correct and required for the Kling Omni path).

> ⚠️ **Latent trap:** all three components fall back to the **pre-2.5 layout**
> when that config fetch fails. The endpoint returns **403 when called
> directly** — it only succeeds through the authenticated frontend proxy — so
> if that proxying ever changes, the whole 2.5 UX silently reverts to
> demanding Kling registration and LoRA training, with no error shown. The
> fallback direction is deliberate (it never hides genuinely-required setup),
> but if the UI unexpectedly shows the old "isn't ready for either video path"
> message, **check this endpoint first**.
